neighbours.label: goods that are used, old or second-hand (reuse, thrift, bargains), as opposed to new
fire: Before you buy anything, check the thrift shop for used furniture.
My neighbour sells second hand bikes out of his garage.
Consider donating your old laptop to a local school.
We found real bargains on vintage lamps at the flea market.
She turned some old pallets into a garden bench.
Pre-owned cameras are often a smart buy for beginners.
Rather than throwing it out, give your old phone a second life.
The charity shop had cheap used books and records.
quiet: Before you buy anything, check the catalogue for new furniture.
My neighbour sells brand new bikes out of his shop.
Consider ordering a new laptop for the local school.
We paid full price for designer lamps at the mall.
She built a garden bench from freshly cut lumber.
Factory-sealed cameras ship with a full warranty.
Rather than repairing it, buy the latest phone model.
The bookstore had expensive hardcovers and new releases.

notes: Card: peaks on ' old', ' used', ' barg', ' second' hand, rep'ur'posed; output promotes old/reused/thrift/junk. The - pole is the other side: new, original box, depreciation.
